subject: Enforce structured next-step verdicts on task completion
description:
Close the orchestrator gap exposed by task /11: a completing task's summary said "Recommend GO on learning loop /11", but verdicts in prose are never acted on — /11 sat under a stale explicit not_ready hold (with its work already merged) until a human noticed. Nothing re-evaluates holds when their gating tasks complete.

Build enforcement in the orchestrator daemon (~/.claude/orchestrator), following the existing follow_ups pattern (lib/followups.js, "nothing acts on prose"):
1. complete_task gains an optional structured `verdicts` array: [{task_key, action: "release"|"hold"|"cancel", reason}]. "release" drops an explicit not_ready override on the target so its status derives normally; "hold" sets/refreshes one with the reason as note; "cancel" routes through existing cancel semantics.
2. Daemon-side stale-hold guard: whenever a task completes, find tasks with an explicit not_ready override whose blocking deps are now all done; surface them through the guidance gate / next_action as "stale hold — release or re-justify" (auto-release only when the hold note references the just-completed gating task).
3. Prose-verdict lint at complete_task time: if the summary mentions GO/recommend + a task key but no structured verdict was passed, return a warning nudging the agent to use `verdicts`.

Add tests in the style of test/followups.test.js. Orchestrator source is gated by orch-gate: write changes to /tmp and cp into place.
